LanguageData.CC_SetNote_DiplomacyFeasts: Feasts, hunts, games and contests with guests from the peoples around, once a season at a home.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_DiplomacyFeasts_Tip: From a people's card, the calendar or at the steward's suggestion, invite up to three notables of peoples at peace who live within three days' travel and think well enough of the colony (regard 0 or more), by letter or call. Each answers by their regard, the road and whether what their people hope for is offered: a hunt for a tribe, a hunt or wrestling in the middle ages, a race or a shooting match for an industrial people, wrestling or a game at the tables for spacers, a fine meal and music for the Empire. On the first fine day after the last of them can arrive, they walk in with one or two of their people and wait by the gate. Up to four contests are held on the map in the afternoon (wrestling by the sparring rules, a race, a hunt, a game at the colony's tables, and a shooting match only where a mod gives targets), the feast is the colony's gathering with the guests at its table, the champion of the day gets the prize, and the guests stay the night and go home at first light. A good welcome raises their regard and their people remember it; an empty plate is a slight. A wrestling bout's blow goes in hard about one time in 25; a guest's night after the feast turns into a fistfight about one guest night in 15. Off: nothing new is planned or suggested, and a feast under way plays out.

LanguageData.CC_Feast_Dlg_Intro: Invite up to {GUESTS} notables of peoples at peace who live within three days' travel and think well enough of the colony. The invitations go out by letter or call; once every answer is in, the day is the first fine one after the last of them can arrive. Up to {CONTESTS} contests are held that afternoon, the feast in the evening, and the guests stay the night.
LanguageData.CC_Feast_Dlg_NoCandidates: The colony knows no notable of a people at peace with it.
LanguageData.CC_Feast_Dlg_GuestNote: Thinks {REGARD} of the colony, {DAYS} days away; hopes for {HOPE}.
LanguageData.CC_Feast_Dlg_GuestTip: {NAME} is likelier to come when {HOPE} is among the contests.
LanguageData.CC_Feast_Dlg_Contest_Wrestling: Bouts between the colony's people and the guests by the sparring rules. A blow goes in hard about one time in 25.
LanguageData.CC_Feast_Dlg_Contest_Race: From the gate to a marker and back at a run. Children may run too.
LanguageData.CC_Feast_Dlg_Contest_Hunt: The colony's hunters and the guests hunt safe game on the colony's land. A beast may turn on its hunter now and then.
LanguageData.CC_Feast_Dlg_Contest_Tables: Games at the colony's tables, the colony's players against the guests.
LanguageData.CC_Feast_Dlg_Contest_Shooting: Five shots each at the colony's target.
LanguageData.CC_Feast_Dlg_ContestTip_Wrestling: Up to three bouts in a ring by the gate, each between one of the colony's grown people and a guest: eight swings each, or until one yields to the pain. One blow in a bout goes in harder than meant about one time in 25 (a cracked rib, a bloody nose gone bad), never on someone hurt in the last three days or with child.
LanguageData.CC_Feast_Dlg_ContestTip_Race: The runners line up at the gate, run out to a marker on open ground and back, and the first home wins. A runner may stumble at the turn and lose a moment.
LanguageData.CC_Feast_Dlg_ContestTip_Hunt: Game nothing likely to turn is marked for hunting, one beast more than there are hunters; the most kills wins. As in any hunt, a beast may turn on its hunter now and then.
LanguageData.CC_Feast_Dlg_ContestTip_Tables: Up to two games, played as the game's own recreation; the winner by the game's own skill for it, and some luck.
LanguageData.CC_Feast_Dlg_ContestTip_Shooting: Each shooter takes five shots from a line ten paces or so from the target; the most hits wins.
LanguageData.CC_Feast_Dlg_PrizeNote: Set aside from the stores until the feast, then carried to the champion of the day. A guest who wins takes it home; a guest given the prize thinks much better of the colony.
LanguageData.CC_Feast_Dlg_Meals: The stores hold {MEALS} cooked meals; about {WANTED} are wanted ({COLONISTS} of the colony's, {GUESTS} guests and those who come with them).
LanguageData.CC_Feast_Dlg_MealsShort: A guest who isn't served a meal at the feast feels slighted, and their people remember it.
LanguageData.CC_Feast_Dlg_Empire: Guests of the Empire expect a fine meal and music: the colony has an instrument, and its best player will play for them.
LanguageData.CC_Feast_Dlg_EmpireNoMusic: Guests of the Empire expect a fine meal and music, and the colony has no instrument to play for them.
LanguageData.CC_Feast_Dlg_Night: The guests stay the night in the colony's beds (guest beds first), or on the floor if there are none to spare. Now and then a guest's night ends in a fistfight with one of the colony's.
LanguageData.CC_Feast_Dlg_SendTip: A letter to each guest (or a call, with a comms console and a people who can take one), written when the writer has a moment.
